verdict.rationale: Rootly's docs describe its own hosted public status pages. A public JSON API served on the status page's custom domain implies custom-domain support, and the API changelog's incident-scoped status-page-events endpoint shows status pages tied to incident state. Nothing documents notifying subscribers. Missing for 10: subscriber notifications (email/SMS/webhook subscriptions), explicit custom-domain setup docs, a detailed description of how incident state propagates to the page, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I can publish a hosted public status page — custom domain, subscriber notifications — driven from incident state

citations.quote: Rootly has two types of status pages available: public status pages and private status pages.
Status pages allow you to quickly communicate information about the health of your services and applications to internal stakeholders and external customers.
Rootly exposes a public JSON API on your status page's custom domain, allowing you to programmatically retrieve current status and incident data.
POST /v1/incidents/{id}/status-page-events on a scheduled maintenance now returns 422 (Invalid status for scheduled) when status is omitted
